title: Dedicated capacity degradation handling and credit computation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define an operationally tractable, auditable, and customer-facing convention for measuring dedicated capacity degradation, automating customer notification, and computing monetary credits. This ticket formalizes: 1) measurement windows and heuristics for distinguishing transient spikes vs sustained capacity degradation; 2) an error-budget accounting model that consumes credits predictably across rolling windows; 3) precise contract-ready language snippets for SOWs and invoices; and 4) integration points with autoscaling policies and fleet controls so the platform can attempt remediation before credits are issued.
acceptance_criteria: A clear definition of measurable capacity delivered vs committed capacity (per-AZ and pooled) that QA can validate with synthetic traffic
An error-budget model and an example credit computation for monthly billing that legal approves as customer-facing language
Automated detection that classifies incidents into transient vs sustained windows using a 3-tier rule set (fast spike, short degradation, sustained degradation)
Notification and remediation playbook integrated with the Console: automatic ticket creation, customer-facing status messages, and ability to opt into expedited autoscale actions
End-to-end tests that simulate degraded capacity and verify credit issuance, notification, and billing adjustments in a sandbox
measurement_method: Measure observed served throughput (tokens/s or requests/s normalized by model class) per dedicated pool per 5-minute interval. Compute the 99th percentile (p99) capacity available during each billing day and compare to the committed baseline capacity for that pool. Use an alignment window of 1 hour to smooth short spikes; sustained degradation is any continuous 4-hour period where the hourly alignment value is below 90% of committed capacity. The platform will record raw counters and an auditable time-series for every decision.
credit_formula: credit = clamp(0, floor(MONTHLY_COMMIT * max(0, 1 - (SUM_OBSERVED_CAPACITY / SUM_COMMITTED_CAPACITY) * ADJUSTMENT)), MONTHLY_COMMIT) where ADJUSTMENT = 0.85 for partial mitigations (e.g., single-AZ), ADJUSTMENT = 1.0 for full-service failures; SUM_* are computed across the billing month but weighted by degradation window length. Example: committed=$100k, observed fraction=0.88, ADJUSTMENT=1 => credit = floor(100000 * (1 - 0.88)) = $12,000 (subject to cap and minimum notice windows). This formula must be represented in plain-English contract language in the SOW appendix.
notification_playbook: T+0: automated incident created in Customer Portal and linked to internal incident; brief note with impacted pool and preliminary measurement
T+15m: automated updated assessment (spike vs trending) and suggested automated autoscale action (if enabled for customer)
T+4h sustained: official degradation notice sent; estimated credit and remediation ETA (if autoscale action in progress include progress %)
Post-incident: formal computation of credit within 7 business days and invoice adjustment in next billing cycle; summary root-cause and mitigations published
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (sandbox): implement measurement pipeline and daily reports for 3 pilot customers
Phase 2 (beta): wire notification playbook + manual credit calculation for 5 customers; collect feedback on wording
Phase 3 (GA): automated calculation + billing integration; publish SOW appendix and update TOS for Dedicated customers
Fallback policy: if automation disagrees with legal/ops review, default to manual adjustment with a 2-week hold period
notes: Legal review required for customer-facing formula wording and cap language
Trade-offs considered: aggressive autoscale vs conservative credit issuance; decided to prefer autoscale + notification as first remediation so credits are a last-resort consumer protection
